corfort.gloss: 40-metal tier-2 wall with 8900 health; stops tier-1 and tier-2 units and low shots; tier-3 plows through
corfort.prose: The Fortification Wall is the tier-2 wall: 40 metal and 500 energy, 8900 health, nearly four times a Dragon's Teeth's (cordrag). It blocks tier-1 and tier-2 units and low-flying projectiles and shields the towers behind it, which fire over it; tier-3 units plow through it and siege weapons arc over it. Only the tier-2 constructors and the Twitcher (corfast) build it.

corfrad.name: Naval Radar / Sonar Tower
corfrad.gloss: 130-metal radar and sonar tower on water, 2100 radar and 900 sonar
corfrad.prose: The Naval Radar / Sonar Tower is the Radar Tower (corrad) for water: 130 metal and 1000 energy, 114 health, 2100 radar and 900 sonar. It is the early warning of a naval base for aircraft, ships and submarines alike. It is the first sensor a sea base builds, and at 114 health the first thing a raid kills.

corfrt.name: Slingshot
corfrt.gloss: the light anti-air tower on water, 80 metal, missiles at 765; early cover for a naval base
corfrt.prose: The Slingshot is the Thistle (corrl) built on water: 80 metal and 850 energy, 335 health, missiles at range 765 for aircraft only. A few protect a naval base from early raids; a swarm gets past one alone. Build it once enemy aircraft have been seen over the water, not before.

corfship.name: Brimstone
corfship.air: 69 dps against aircraft (18% of its ground damage)
corfship.gloss: tier-2 anti-swarm ship, speed 93, flamethrower at 450 and anti-air; burns infrastructure and raiders, loses to cruisers and subs
corfship.prose: The Brimstone is the fast tier-2 raider: 630 metal, 2700 health, speed 93, a flamethrower at range 450 doing about 375 damage a second plus anti-air missiles at 710. It burns naval infrastructure and hunts high-value ships such as missile boats; it loses to cruisers, to advanced torpedo launchers, and to submarines it can only outrun. Its flamethrower burns groups of light craft close in, which is what makes it the anti-swarm ship rather than a line ship.

corfus.name: Fusion Reactor
corfus.gloss: tier-2 fusion, 850 energy a second for 3600 metal; dense steady energy, follows the extractor upgrades; explodes
corfus.prose: The Fusion Reactor makes 850 energy a second for 3600 metal and 22000 energy, with 4300 health and 2500 energy storage; only the tier-2 constructors build it, at 59000 build time (four and a half minutes for one advanced constructor, so it needs helpers). At 4.2 metal per energy a second it is no cheaper than advanced solar or wind on a windy map; its value is density, steadiness and builder time, which is why it follows the extractor upgrades rather than preceding them. It is a favourite bomber target and it explodes when destroyed, so it stands apart from the base under anti-air.

corgant.name: Experimental Gantry
corgant.gloss: tier-3 gantry, 8400 metal, 1800 build power; makes the Juggernaut, Behemoth, Karganeth, Demon, Catapult, Shiva, Cataphract
corgant.prose: The Experimental Gantry is the tier-3 factory: 8400 metal and 62000 energy, 17800 health, 1800 build power, making the Juggernaut (corkorg), Karganeth, Behemoth, Shiva, Catapult, Cataphract and Demon. An advanced constructor builds it. It is a late-game decision: the gantry and its first unit are a tier-2 economy's whole output for minutes, and each unit it makes is a single point of failure to EMP, bombers or a D-gun.

corgantuw.name: Experimental Gantry
corgantuw.gloss: tier-3 gantry under water, 8350 metal; makes the amphibious experimentals: Juggernaut, Shiva, Cataphract, Poison Arrow, Salamander
corgantuw.prose: The underwater Experimental Gantry is the sea version of the gantry (corgant): 8350 metal and 62500 energy, 17800 health, 1800 build power, built on the sea floor by the Advanced Construction Sub (coracsub), making the Juggernaut, Shiva, Salamander, Poison Arrow and Cataphract. It is offered only where the builder reaches deep water. Its units arrive from the sea floor, which is the reason to build it rather than the land gantry.

corgarp.name: Garpike
corgarp.air: 17 dps against aircraft (22% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corgarp.gloss: tier-1 amphibious tank; drives the sea floor to hit shoreline targets by surprise; loses to land tanks
corgarp.prose: The Garpike is a 220-metal amphibious tank (1420 health, speed 58.5) with a 116-damage cannon every 1.5 seconds at range 305 and 175 sonar. It drives along the sea floor and up hills like a bot, so it surprises undefended targets near a shore; it is weaker than the land tanks in a straight exchange and loses to turrets. It takes only a fifth of EMP damage. A Muskrat (cormuskrat) along with it reclaims the wrecks.

corgate.name: Overseer
corgate.gloss: 3200-metal plasma shield, radius 550; stops plasma artillery and cannon shells, not bombs, lasers or missiles
corgate.prose: The Overseer is a shield generator: 3200 metal and 55000 energy, 3550 health, a plasma shield of radius 550 that absorbs projectile fire and regenerates for 562 energy a second, more than half a fusion. It deflects plasma artillery and long-range cannon shells and takes a great deal before it drops; bombs, lasers and missiles pass straight through it. A few around a base answer an artillery barrage.

corgator.name: Incisor
corgator.air: 18 dps against aircraft (19% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corgator.gloss: fast tier-1 light tank (speed 85), laser at 230; raids economy, beats Pawns and rocket bots; dies to towers
corgator.prose: The Incisor is the tier-1 light tank: 120 metal, 820 health, speed 85, a 75-damage laser every 0.8 seconds at range 230 with no energy cost. It kills extractors, constructors and radar, beats Pawns (armpw) and rocket bots, which it beat in equal-metal duels, and massed it ambushes a commander. It loses to towers, to the Pounder (corlevlr) and, at equal metal, to the Mace (armham); its sight is short, so it walks into things, and it is slower than the Blitz (armflash) but outranges it.

corgeo.name: Geothermal Powerplant
corgeo.gloss: 300 energy a second for 540 metal, only on a steam vent; explodes when killed
corgeo.prose: The Geothermal Powerplant makes 300 energy a second for 540 metal and 13000 energy, 2050 health, and can stand only on one of the map's steam vents. Where a vent is safe it is a tier-1 economy's biggest single generator; a tier-1 constructor builds it. It explodes when destroyed, and it is a target worth a raid.

corgol.name: Tzar
corgol.gloss: 1650-metal superheavy tank, 900-damage wide-splash plasma at 650; deletes tier-1 groups; blind past 395
corgol.prose: The Tzar is a superheavy tier-2 tank: 1650 metal, 7800 health, speed 39, a 900-damage plasma shell every 3.5 seconds at range 650 with a large splash. It goes through groups of tier-1 units and light defences, and it sees only 395, so it needs a spotter to use its range; the Banisher (corban) outranges it. It is a heavy transport's cargo rather than a walker, and its wreck is worth nearly 900 metal to whoever reclaims it, so do not lose it.

corhal.name: Halberd
corhal.air: 31 dps against aircraft (9% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corhal.gloss: tier-1 assault hovertank with tier-2 weight: 4350 health, 344 dps beam at 300 for 45 energy a shot
corhal.prose: The Halberd is a heavy hovertank from a tier-1 platform: 640 metal, 4350 health, speed 45, a beam laser doing 344 damage a second at range 300 for 45 energy a shot, about 93 a second firing. It soaks damage for a hover force and kills anything that comes close, a Dolphin (armdecade) in four shots, and it is immune to torpedoes. Its range and turning are poor, so it is an escort and assault unit, softened up for by Mangonels (cormh); it needs the energy.

corhllt.name: Twin Guard
corhllt.air: 21 dps against aircraft (7% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corhllt.gloss: 195-metal double laser tower, 321 dps with lasers at 490 and 400; out-ranges rocket bots, shreds swarms
corhllt.prose: The Twin Guard is two light lasers stacked on one tower: 195 metal and 1750 energy, 1670 health, each beam 75 damage every half second (321 a second together), the top gun at range 490 and the bottom at 400, 15 energy a shot each. Its top gun out-reaches the rocket bots (475), so a rocket group cannot kill it for free, and its two independent guns shred a swarm; it is a serious threat to a commander that walks into it. It stops in an energy stall, and a heavy transport can move it.

corhlt.name: Warden
corhlt.air: 29 dps against aircraft (13% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corhlt.gloss: 480-metal heavy laser tower, 218 dps at 620, 2750 health; out-ranges every tier-1 unit but artillery
corhlt.prose: The Warden is the tier-1 heavy laser tower: 480 metal and 4700 energy, 2750 health, a 261-damage beam every 1.2 seconds (218 a second) at range 620, 50 energy a shot. It out-ranges every tier-1 land unit except the artillery vehicles (710) and the tier-2 skirmishers, so it kills rocket bots, missile trucks and the support bots behind a line, and it out-ranges enemy laser towers; it fires lighter and faster than the Overwatch (armhlt), which suits it against infantry. A single one alone is a target for Wolverines (corwolv); it needs cheaper towers and units beside it, and it stops in an energy stall. Counting a turret as about three times its metal in a fight is the rule the record supports.

corhp.name: Hovercraft Platform
corhp.gloss: tier-1 hovercraft platform on land, 670 metal; makes the construction hovercraft, Goon, Cayman, Mangonel, Halberd, Birdeater
corhp.prose: The Hovercraft Platform is the land-built hovercraft factory: 670 metal and 2000 energy, 3750 health, 150 build power, making the Construction Hovercraft (corch), Goon, Cayman, Birdeater, Mangonel and the heavy Halberd. Hovercraft cross land and water alike, so the platform is the answer on a map where the enemy is across water and a shipyard is not wanted; its units are dearer than bots for what they fight. It is offered on any ground the builder can reach, unlike the shipyard, and its units are the only tier-1 way to reach an island economy without ships.

corhrk.name: Arbiter
corhrk.gloss: tier-2 vertical-launch rocket bot, 1210 range, 800 damage; hits behind cliffs and walls; 610 health
corhrk.prose: The Arbiter fires an 800-damage rocket straight up every 8 seconds that comes down at range 1210, over walls and cliffs: 600 metal, 610 health, speed 54. It outranges every turret including the plasma batteries and breaks a defended line from far away; it also has almost no health and its rocket is slow, so it needs a screen and it misses anything that moves. In the simulated study an Arbiter army was the worst Cortex mix (-0.79) for lack of health, though the simulator handles its arc badly; a handful behind Sumos (corcan) is the sound use.

corhunt.name: Watcher
corhunt.gloss: tier-1 radar and sonar seaplane, 2200 radar and 900 sonar at speed 324; scouts the sea; unarmed
corhunt.prose: The Watcher is an unarmed radar and sonar seaplane: 130 metal, 730 health, speed 324, 2200 radar and 900 sonar. It scouts the sea and shows a fleet what is in the air, on the water and under it. Fighters kill it.

corhurc.name: Hailstorm
corhurc.air: 238 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corhurc.gloss: tier-2 heavy bomber, five 333-damage bombs; three take a fusion in a pass; dies to fighters and flak
corhurc.prose: The Hailstorm is the tier-2 bomber: 310 metal, 1520 health, speed 248, a run of five 333-damage bombs. It is for buildings: three kill a Fusion Reactor (corfus) in one pass, and laid across an army's path it hurts units too. It is stronger and dearer than the Blizzard (armpnix); fighters and flak kill it, so scout and escort.

corhvytrans.name: Hephaestus
corhvytrans.gloss: tier-1 heavy air transport; carries the commander, heavy units and light turrets; slow and lightly armoured
corhvytrans.prose: The Hephaestus is the heavy transport: 190 metal, 800 health, speed 100, carries one unit including the commander, heavy tier-2 units and light turrets (Guard, Twin Guard, Thistle, radar tower), so it can put a turret down without a constructor. It is slow for an aircraft and dies with its cargo to fighters or flak. It is the cheapest way to move something slow across the map.

corint.name: Basilisk
corint.gloss: 4600-metal long-range cannon, 2000 damage at 4950 for 6000 energy a shot; shells across the map; a priority target
corint.prose: The Basilisk is the long-range plasma cannon: 4600 metal and 67000 energy, 4700 health, a 2000-damage shell every 16 seconds at range 4950 for 6000 energy, with a large splash. It reaches across most maps, wrecks packed formations, and out-ranges any ship or amphibious unit, so it is the battery that takes back a sea; it fires slower than the Basilica (armbrtha) with more punch. An Overseer (corgate) shield stops its shells at a large energy cost to the shielder. Once built it is the enemy's first target.

corjamt.name: Castro
corjamt.gloss: 100-metal jammer tower, hides units within 360 from enemy radar for 25 energy a second; unarmed
corjamt.prose: The Castro is the tier-1 jammer tower: 100 metal and 4500 energy, 1070 health, hiding everything within 360 from enemy radar for 25 energy a second. Overlapped over a position or an army group it keeps them off the radar that artillery targets by; line of sight still sees through it. It is cheaper than Armada's Sneaky Pete (armjamt) with a shorter reach and more health.

corjugg.name: Behemoth
corjugg.air: 621 dps against aircraft (55% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corjugg.gloss: 20000-metal walking turret: disintegrator at 590, beam lasers; 335000 health, speed 16; no anti-air
corjugg.prose: The Behemoth is a walking fortress with 335000 health at speed 16.5: 20000 metal, a disintegrator gun at range 590 that kills a heavy tank in one shot, and three beam lasers. It spearheads an endgame assault on fortifications and kills tier-3 units that come near it. Anything that outranges it shoots it for free, it has no anti-air, and EMP stops it; it needs an escort for its flanks and the energy for its lasers.

corjuno.name: Juno
corjuno.gloss: 660-metal Juno launcher; stockpiled pulses blow up radar, jammers, mines and scout swarms in a huge area; manual fire
corjuno.prose: The Juno stockpiles anti-electronics missiles: 660 metal and 16000 energy, 2500 health, each missile 12000 energy and 75 seconds, fired by hand at range 32000 into a huge area where for about 25 seconds radar units, jammers, mines, cameras and scout spam like Rascals (corfav) explode. It is the answer to a minefield or a scout-spam opening and it clears the enemy's radar before a strike; friendly electronics in the blast die too, and spy bots are immune. It cloaks.

corkarg.name: Karganeth
corkarg.air: 250 dps against aircraft (42% of its ground damage)
corkarg.gloss: 2500-metal all-terrain assault mech; homing missiles at 700 and anti-air; kills single units, weak vs groups
corkarg.prose: The Karganeth is a 2500-metal all-terrain mech: 12500 health, speed 45, rapid homing missiles at range 700 plus twin anti-air launchers. It climbs cliffs and kills single units quickly, aircraft included; without any area weapon it does poorly against groups, and a massed tier-2 army out-trades it. It is the gantry's flexible mid-cost unit for hilly ground.

corkorg.name: Juggernaut
corkorg.air: 2188 dps against aircraft (52% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corkorg.gloss: 29000-metal experimental walker; plasma, rockets and a 5500-damage laser at 900; loses to massed range and D-guns
corkorg.prose: The Juggernaut is Cortex's most powerful land unit: 29000 metal, 149000 health, speed 37, a plasma shotgun, vertical rockets and a 5500-damage laser at range 900 that costs 1200 energy a shot; it makes 300 energy itself and walks the sea floor. It can take several Titans (armbanth) at once. Massed long-range fire (Pulsars, Starlights), a Behemoth (corjugg) up close and a commander's D-gun kill it; when it dies its blast is nearly a nuke, so keep your own army away. It is a whole tier-2 economy in one unit from the Experimental Gantry (corgant).

corlab.name: Bot Lab
corlab.gloss: tier-1 bot factory, 470 metal, 150 build power; makes the constructor, Grunt, Thug, Aggravator, Trasher, Graverobber
corlab.prose: The Bot Lab is the usual first factory: 470 metal and 1050 energy, 2900 health, 150 build power, and it makes the six tier-1 bots: Construction Bot (corck), Grunt, Aggravator, Thug, Trasher and Graverobber; Cortex has no tier-1 scout bot and no heavy brawler. It draws about 80 energy a second while building, so a lab started before any generator empties the store and then builds at a crawl; a solar first, then the lab, is the shape that works. Its 150 build power turns into about 10 metal a second of bots, so an income above that needs a second lab or construction turrets. It is the opponent's favourite raid target after extractors.

corlevlr.name: Pounder
corlevlr.gloss: tier-1 riot tank; beats every tier-1 land unit at equal metal; slow (40), loses only to being outranged
corlevlr.prose: The Pounder is the strongest tier-1 land unit in a straight fight: 220 metal, 1400 health, speed 40, a 190-damage plasma blast every 1.8 seconds at range 315 that knocks light units back. In equal-metal duels it beat every other tier-1 land unit at every formation spacing, Pawns (armpw) and Blitzes (armflash) most of all, with the Janus (armjanus) and light turrets its closest matchups. It is the slowest thing in the table and Rocketeers (armrock, 475), artillery (710) and anything that kites it can shoot it without reply, though that needs stand-off the duels did not have. It cannot shoot over other units, so stagger a line of them; with Dragon's Teeth it makes a choke a kill zone. Never send Pawn or Mace balls into scouted Pounders.

corllt.name: Guard
corllt.air: 11 dps against aircraft (7% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corllt.gloss: 90-metal light laser tower, 161 dps at 435, 20 energy a shot; stops raiders, out-ranged by rockets
corllt.prose: The Guard is the light laser tower: 90 metal and 700 energy, 650 health, a 75-damage beam every half second (161 a second) at range 435, 20 energy a shot. One beside an extractor is the cheapest way to stop a lone raider, and the opponent builds one beside nearly all of its own; where the fight's place is known a tower out-trades units, and where the enemy can walk round it it is wasted. It pays energy for every shot, so in a stall it stops firing, and a line of them fires only as fast as energy arrives. Rocketeers (armrock) and Aggravators (corstorm) out-range it by 40 and kill it from safety, a Lasher (cormist) does so untouched, Maces (armham) and Thugs (corthud) overpower it at equal metal, and Grunts (corak) and Pawns (armpw) lose to it.

cormabm.name: Saviour
cormabm.gloss: mobile anti-nuke tank; stockpiles interceptors to protect an army from nuclear missiles; unarmed
cormabm.prose: The Saviour is a 1250-metal mobile anti-nuke with 870 health and speed 51. It stockpiles interceptor missiles (150 metal and 6500 energy each, 90 seconds a missile, up to 20) and shoots down nuclear missiles aimed within its cover, which is longer than the all-terrain Umbrella's (armscab). Late in a game one with the army means the army cannot be nuked; lower its stockpile limit so it does not eat resources. It has no other weapon.

cormadsam.name: SAM
cormadsam.gloss: 350-metal hardened anti-air missile battery at 950, 2500 health; kills bombers and gunships quickly; nothing against ground
cormadsam.prose: The SAM is the mid-cost anti-air battery: 350 metal and 5500 energy, 2500 health, fast missiles at range 950 for aircraft only. It kills bombers rapidly and is a serious threat to gunships, stronger and tougher than the same metal of Thistles (corrl), with a quick build; the Eradicator (corerad) reaches further and flak kills groups. Against ground it does nothing.

cormakr.name: Energy Converter
cormakr.gloss: converts 70 energy a second into 1 metal for 1 metal to build; for surplus energy only, chains explosions
cormakr.prose: The Energy Converter turns 70 energy a second into 1 metal a second, for 1 metal and 1250 energy, 167 health. It is for energy that would otherwise sit at a full store: extractors beat converters while free spots remain, and metal in the bank is better spent on a second lab or a construction turret than on converters. A cluster of them explodes in a chain when one dies, so spread them, and aim at the enemy's clusters for the same reason.

cormando.name: Commando
cormando.air: 60 dps against aircraft (30% of its ground damage)
cormando.gloss: 1200-metal paratrooper engineer: laser at 300, short jammer, 200 build power, survives a shot-down transport
cormando.prose: The Commando is a 1200-metal raider-engineer: 1800 health, speed 75, a 100-damage laser twice a second at range 300, a 150-range radar jammer, amphibious, with 200 build power for mines, cameras and reclaiming. It survives being dropped when its transport is shot down, which is what it is for: landing behind a base, mining it, wounding buildings and reclaiming them for their metal. It is not a line unit; a real army kills it.

cormart.name: Quaker
cormart.gloss: tier-2 mobile artillery, 420-damage shells with 72 splash at 800; kills packed groups and towers; helpless if reached
cormart.prose: The Quaker is tier-2 artillery: 400 metal, 1200 health, speed 58, a 420-damage shell every 5 seconds at range 800 with a 72 splash. It shells packed formations and turret lines from beyond their reach and is more reliable against groups than the Mauser (armmart); it fires only over its front, and anything that reaches it kills it. Keep it behind Tigers (correap) with radar to spot.

cormaw.name: Dragon's Maw
cormaw.gloss: 290-metal pop-up flamethrower turret at 410 that looks like a wall when down; burns packed units at a choke
cormaw.prose: The Dragon's Maw is a pop-up flamethrower turret: 290 metal and 1550 energy, 1610 health, a flame burst doing 320 damage a second at range 410 across everything in its cone, with no energy cost. Popped down it looks like a block of Dragon's Teeth (cordrag) and is nearly impossible to shell, so bunkered into a wall at a choke it surprises a massed push; clustered, several stop a tank assault. Anything that out-ranges 410 shells it while it is up.

cormex.name: Metal Extractor
cormex.gloss: tier-1 metal extractor on a metal spot, 50 metal; the economy, and the first thing raiders kill
cormex.prose: The Metal Extractor sits on a metal spot and yields what the spot gives, about 2 metal a second on the maps played here, for 50 metal and 500 energy, with 275 health and 3 energy a second upkeep. Extractors are the whole tier-1 income and they beat converters while free spots remain, so expansion is claiming spots as fast as the army can cover them; they are also the first thing every raid goes for, and the opponent puts a turret beside nearly every one of its own. It self-destructs in one second and the blast kills light units beside it. Upgrading it in place to an Advanced Metal Extractor (cormoho) quadruples the spot.

cormexp.name: Advanced Exploiter
cormexp.air: 132 dps against aircraft (21% of its ground damage)
cormexp.gloss: 2400-metal armed advanced extractor, four times the yield with a Mammoth's beam and rockets at 650, 7800 health
cormexp.prose: The Advanced Exploiter is an advanced extractor with a Mammoth's beam laser and a rocket battery at range 650: 2400 metal and 12000 energy, 7800 health, four times a spot's yield, 20 energy a second upkeep and 50 energy a shot for the beam. It holds a front-line spot against a tier-1 army on its own; it costs nearly four advanced extractors, so it is for the one spot that is both rich and contested. Only the tier-2 constructors build it.

cormh.name: Mangonel
cormh.gloss: tier-1 hover rocket launcher, 550 damage at 700 over walls every 9 s; kills turrets before a landing
cormh.prose: The Mangonel is a light hovercraft with a vertical rocket launcher: 200 metal, 550 health, speed 64, a 550-damage rocket every 9 seconds at range 700 that comes down over walls and terrain. It kills turrets and softens an expansion before a hover assault, and its single big hit often leaves no wreck to reclaim. Close-combat units kill it; keep it behind Caymans (corsnap) or a Halberd (corhal).

cormine1.name: Light Mine
cormine1.gloss: 7-metal cloaked mine; kills a light unit that walks on it, 1 energy a second to stay hidden
cormine1.prose: The Light Mine is a 7-metal cloaked mine (1 energy a second to stay cloaked, invisible to radar) that explodes when a unit passes over it and damages the units nearby. It kills raiders and light bots outright and is laid across the lanes they use, by a Trapper (cormlv); keep your own units off it. Only the minelayer and the decoy commander build it.

cormine2.name: Medium Mine
cormine2.gloss: 25-metal cloaked mine with a wider blast; kills heavier bots and medium tanks; chains with its neighbours
cormine2.prose: The Medium Mine is a 25-metal cloaked mine (2 energy a second) with a wider blast than the light mine's, meant for heavier bots and medium tanks on a tier-1 or early tier-2 push. Laid too close together they chain-explode, and they hurt your own units badly; a Trapper (cormlv), a Twitcher (corfast), a Commando (cormando) or the decoy commander lays them. It is the mine for a lane the enemy's Stouts (armstump) or Maces (armham) use, where a light mine would not kill.

cormine3.name: Heavy Mine
cormine3.gloss: 50-metal cloaked heavy mine, three times a medium mine, 330 blast; blunts a packed push at a choke
cormine3.prose: The Heavy Mine is a 50-metal cloaked mine (6 energy a second) with about three times a medium mine's power and a 330-wide blast, for a massed push through a choke; with Dragon's Teeth (cordrag) narrowing the gap it wipes a packed group of plasma bots or medium tanks in one blast. It is poor against a single fast raider, it chains other mines, and it hits friends. A Trapper (cormlv) or the decoy commander lays it.

cormist.name: Lasher
cormist.air: 48 dps against aircraft, its full damage
cormist.gloss: tier-1 missile truck, 575 range against ground and homing missiles at 700 against air; kills light towers untouched
cormist.prose: The Lasher is a light missile truck: 155 metal, 860 health, speed 52, a ground rocket at range 575 doing 63 damage every 2.5 seconds and a homing anti-air missile at 700. Its range beats the light towers by a wide margin: in equal-metal duels it killed Sentries (armllt) and Guards (corllt) without a scratch, and packs of it wear down heavy laser towers. Blitzes (armflash) and fast infantry kill it in close, so keep it at range with a fight order behind Pounders (corlevlr) or Brutes (corraid). It is the vehicle plant's anti-air.

cormls.name: Pathfinder
cormls.gloss: tier-2 naval engineer, 200 build power; builds tier-1 ships in the field, naval turrets and mines; unarmed
cormls.prose: The Pathfinder is a naval engineer: 200 metal, 1600 health, speed 58, 200 build power, no weapon. It builds tier-1 ships (Oppressor, Riptide) where the fleet is, floating construction turrets and naval mines, and assists tier-2 constructors. A minefield laid after taking the sea holds hovercraft off an area until the tier-2 fleet arrives.

cormlv.name: Trapper
cormlv.gloss: stealthy minelayer; lays light, medium and heavy mines, walls and cameras; hides from radar; no real gun
cormlv.prose: The Trapper is a 65-metal minelayer with 450 health, speed 69, radar stealth and a 5-damage bolt that clears mines. It lays the three mine sizes (cormine1, cormine2, cormine3), Dragon's Teeth walls and Beholder cameras, all cloaked and drawing energy. A minefield across a raiding lane kills light units outright and hurts anything heavier; keep your own units off it. It repairs but cannot assist construction, and it cannot fight.

cormmkr.name: Advanced Energy Converter
cormmkr.gloss: tier-2 converter, 600 energy a second into 10.3 metal for 370 metal; barely better than tier 1
cormmkr.prose: The Advanced Energy Converter turns 600 energy a second into 10.3 metal a second (58 energy a metal) for 370 metal and 21000 energy, 560 health. It is only about 17 percent more energy-efficient than the tier-1 converter (70 energy a metal); its gain is capacity in one building, so it is for a fusion-sized surplus late in a game, not a reason to go tier 2. Only the tier-2 constructors build it, and clusters chain-explode.

cormoho.name: Advanced Metal Extractor
cormoho.gloss: tier-2 extractor upgrade, 640 metal, four times the spot's yield for 20 energy a second; the first tier-2 buy
cormoho.prose: The Advanced Metal Extractor replaces a tier-1 extractor on its spot: 640 metal and 8100 energy, 3900 health, four times the yield (0.004 against 0.001 a spot unit), 20 energy a second upkeep, 600 metal storage. One upgrade adds about three extractors' worth of income and repays its metal in around 100 seconds, so upgrading the safest spots first is what the advanced constructor (corack) is for; five upgrades roughly double a tier-1 income. Only the tier-2 constructors build it. With nothing banked and other builders drawing, an upgrade takes minutes instead of its nominal 70 seconds, so give the constructor helpers or a bank.

cormort.name: Sheldon
cormort.gloss: tier-2 mortar bot, 850 range; wears down turret lines from safety; 940 health, dies to anything that closes
cormort.prose: The Sheldon is a mobile mortar: 400 metal, 940 health, speed 50, a 105-damage shell every 1.6 seconds lobbed to range 850, further than any tower short of the plasma batteries. It chips at static lines from where they cannot answer and supports a close-range front; on its own it is paper, and fodder like Ticks (armflea) and Pawns (armpw) run it down. In the simulated tier-2 study a Sheldon army was one of the two worst Cortex mixes (-0.58) because it has no health; use a few behind Sumos (corcan), never as the army. It fires further than it sees, so pair it with a radar bot.

cormship.name: Messenger
cormship.air: 69 dps against aircraft (50% of its ground damage)
cormship.gloss: tier-2 cruise missile ship, 1100-damage rockets at 1550 over terrain, ignore shields; levels a shore base
cormship.prose: The Messenger is the shore bombardment ship: 2000 metal, 3350 health, speed 61, cruise missiles doing 1100 damage every 8 seconds at range 1550 on a high arc that clears hills and ignores plasma shields, plus a secondary anti-air launcher. It outranges every land defence and levels a base in a few volleys; a Phantasm (corsjam) jammer beside it keeps it off radar until it fires. Intercepting the ships or tactical nukes are the answers.

cormstor.name: Metal Storage
cormstor.gloss: 3000 metal storage for 340 metal; banks metal for a tier-2 lab or an upgrade burst; explodes when killed
cormstor.prose: The Metal Storage adds 3000 metal storage for 340 metal and 590 energy, 2100 health. A store holds the bank that starts an advanced lab or a run of extractor upgrades without stalling everything else; at tier 1 a full store is usually a sign to build a second lab instead. It explodes when destroyed and clusters chain.

cormuskrat.name: Muskrat
cormuskrat.gloss: amphibious tier-1 constructor, 85 build power; builds on land and the sea floor, including naval buildings; unarmed
cormuskrat.prose: The Muskrat is a 170-metal amphibious constructor (1110 health, speed 40.5, 85 build power) that builds on land and under water and has the naval buildings on its list: shipyard, torpedo launcher, tidal generator, hovercraft platform, plus the land base; it climbs steeper hills than other vehicles. It is the builder for a map with water and expands between islands. Torpedoes, submarines and destroyers kill it under water; raiders kill it on land.

cornanotc.name: Construction Turret
cornanotc.gloss: 200-build-power construction turret, 230 metal; assists, repairs and reclaims within its reach; unarmed
cornanotc.prose: The Construction Turret is 200 build power that does not move: 230 metal and 3200 energy, 560 health, assisting, repairing and reclaiming anything within its radius, and by default it reclaims enemy units that come into reach. Two or three beside a lab more than double its output, which is the right use of banked metal before a second lab; a Hercules (corvalk) can carry one to wherever build power is needed. One dying damages the turrets beside it, so do not pack them.

cornanotcplat.name: Naval Construction Turret
cornanotcplat.gloss: the construction turret built on water, 200 build power for 230 metal
cornanotcplat.prose: The Naval Construction Turret is the Construction Turret (cornanotc) built on water: 200 build power for 230 metal and 3200 energy, 560 health, assisting, repairing and reclaiming within its radius. Two beside a shipyard double its output. Like the land turret it is 200 build power for 230 metal, and its death damages the turrets beside it.

cornecro.name: Graverobber
cornecro.gloss: 200-build-power repair and resurrection bot; cannot build or fight, follows the army, hides from radar
cornecro.prose: The Graverobber is a 130-metal support bot with 200 build power that repairs, reclaims and resurrects but cannot build. Resurrecting a wreck restores the whole unit for energy only, so one or two behind a fight turn the enemy's dead, and yours, into new units; this is also how the opponent fields your own tier-2 units after a failed push. It has 220 health, no weapon, and is invisible to radar, so it lives only out of sight; keep it behind the line and pull it back when the line goes.

corparrow.name: Poison Arrow
corparrow.gloss: tier-2 very heavy amphibious tank, 6300 health, 370-damage cannon at 575; crosses water and climbs like a bot
corparrow.prose: The Poison Arrow is a 1050-metal amphibious heavy tank: 6300 health, speed 51, a 370-damage cannon every 1.8 seconds at range 575, bot-like slope tolerance and 289 sonar. It arrives from the water or over rough ground and kills the groups sent to stop an amphibious landing; tier-2 skirmishers and assault tanks beat it head on. It takes a fifth of EMP damage. Bring Trashers (corcrash) or Manticores (coraak) for air cover under water and Muskrats (cormuskrat) to repair and reclaim.

corplat.name: Seaplane Platform
corplat.gloss: tier-1 seaplane platform under water, 1400 metal; makes the construction seaplane, Cutlass, Dam Buster, Monsoon, Bat, Watcher
corplat.prose: The Seaplane Platform sits on the sea floor and rises to work: 1400 metal and 5500 energy, 2200 health, 300 build power, 800 sonar, making the Construction Seaplane (corcsa), Cutlass, Dam Buster, Monsoon, Bat and Watcher. It is the air factory for a sea map, offered only where the builder reaches deep water. Seaplanes land on and rise from the water, so a base with no land can still fly scouts, bombers and fighters.

corpship.name: Riptide
corpship.air: 39 dps against aircraft (32% of its ground damage)
corpship.gloss: tier-1 assault frigate, plasma at 480, 2350 health; beats destroyers two to one, no anti-submarine weapon
corpship.prose: The Riptide is the frigate: 420 metal, 2350 health, speed 82.5, a plasma cannon doing 120 damage a second at range 480. In numbers it beats destroyers by range and mobility, cost-effective at two to one, and it is tougher and dearer than the Ellysaw (armpship). It has nothing against submarines and nothing against aircraft.

corpt.name: Herring
corpt.air: 60 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corpt.gloss: tier-1 missile corvette, rockets at 650 and anti-air at 750, sonar; harasses builders, loses to any warship
corpt.prose: The Herring is the light missile boat: 210 metal, 890 health, speed 69, a rocket at range 650 doing 24 damage a second, an anti-air missile at 750, 400 sonar and 1000 radar. It harasses expanding constructors, kills inland extractors near the shore until destroyers arrive, outranges torpedo launchers and shoots down drones and gunships; against a Dolphin (armdecade) or any real warship it is hopeless. Never build many.

corpun.name: Agitator
corpun.gloss: 1300-metal plasma battery, 350-damage shells at 1245; kills extractors, radar and turrets behind the line; needs a spotter
corpun.prose: The Agitator is the tier-1 plasma artillery battery: 1300 metal and 13500 energy, 3250 health, a 350-damage shell every 3.2 seconds at range 1245 with a wide splash, switching between a flat and a high arc to hit behind obstacles. It out-ranges every unit and turret short of the long-range cannons and it is what shells the enemy's forward extractors, radar, jammers and construction turrets once the front is set; it needs scouts or radar to see that far. It is a lot of tier-1 metal that does not move; reclaim it when its targets are gone. The opponent's medium setting builds one or two of these only around minute 30.

corpyro.name: Fiend
corpyro.gloss: fast tier-2 flamethrower raider; 240 dps at 230, arms its self-destruct in a second; loses to towers and gunships
corpyro.prose: The Fiend is the tier-2 raider: 200 metal, 1060 health, speed 82, a flamethrower doing about 240 damage a second at range 230 that burns everything in its cone. It kills raiders, light bots, constructors and economy quickly and can be run into a packed group and self-destructed (it arms in one second) for 1110 damage around it. It loses to heavy turrets and to gunships, and the flame's short reach means it takes fire on the way in; a Deceiver (corspec) hides a Fiend party from radar until it strikes. The community pairs it with Sheldons (cormort) as the tough front.

corrad.name: Radar Tower
corrad.gloss: 60-metal radar tower, 2100 radar, 680 sight; shows what moves within range as dots; jammed, blocked by hills
corrad.prose: The Radar Tower shows every enemy unit within 2100 as a radar dot, for 60 metal and 630 energy, 180 health, with 680 sight of its own. It is the early warning for raids and air and the eyes for anything that fires further than it sees; the record shows most games with the enemy base found late, and a radar on an approach fixes that cheaply. Hills block it, a jammer hides units from it and cloaked units do not show. A Hephaestus (corhvytrans) can carry one forward.

corraid.name: Brute
corraid.air: 15 dps against aircraft (19% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corraid.gloss: tier-1 medium tank, 2000 health, plasma at 350; the vehicle line unit, loses to Maces and Pounders
corraid.prose: The Brute is the armoured core of a tier-1 vehicle army: 235 metal, 2000 health, speed 72, a 97-damage shot every 1.2 seconds at range 350. It has the health to lead a push and the speed to arrive together on open ground, and packs of them raid a base alone. In equal-metal duels it lost to the Mace (armham) and badly to the Pounder (corlevlr), while beating the Pawn (armpw) and Rocketeer (armrock); it is the answer to raiders and light defences, with Lashers (cormist) or Wolverines (corwolv) behind it. The commander's D-gun, pop-up lightning turrets and mines kill Brute packs.

correap.name: Tiger
correap.gloss: tier-2 heavy tank, 5300 health, 156 dps at 410; a brick with a gun, cheaper than the Bull
correap.prose: The Tiger is the general-purpose tier-2 tank: 690 metal, 5300 health, speed 69, a 109-damage shot every 0.7 seconds at range 410. It is cheaper and tougher than the Bull (armbull) and holds a front line; its range is short for tier 2 and it has little splash, so Banishers (corban) behind it cover the reach it lacks and Graverobbers (cornecro) keep it repaired. In the simulated tier-2 study the heavy tanks were not tested against the opponent's army, so its worth against a tower line is unmeasured here.

correcl.name: Death Cavalry
correcl.gloss: stealthy resurrection submarine; repairs, reclaims and resurrects wrecks under water; unarmed
correcl.prose: The Death Cavalry is the naval support sub: 240 metal, 420 health, speed 66, submerged and unseen without sonar, with 150 build power to repair, reclaim and resurrect wrecks. Resurrection costs half the unit's energy cost and no metal, so one behind a sea fight turns the wrecks into a fleet. It has no weapon.

corrl.name: Thistle
corrl.gloss: 80-metal light anti-air tower, missiles at 765; stops scouts and light aircraft, nothing against ground; needs radar
corrl.prose: The Thistle is the light anti-air tower: 80 metal and 850 energy, 335 health, missiles at range 765 that do full damage to aircraft and nothing worth counting to anything else. A few around a base or an extractor line stop Finches (corfink), gunships and lone bombers; its rate of fire is low, so a swarm gets through unless several stand together, and it fires further than it sees, so radar coverage makes it work. Build it only after enemy aircraft or an aircraft plant have been seen.

corroach.name: Bedbug
corroach.gloss: amphibious crawling bomb; walks to a target and explodes, harder if self-destructed; spread them out
corroach.prose: The Bedbug is a 69-metal crawling bomb with 620 health, speed 76, that crosses water. It has no gun; it walks into a packed group or a building and explodes, and the blast on a self-destruct order is larger than when it is shot. Spread a swarm out or one going off takes the rest. It is for tank clusters, turret nests and things that cannot shoot it before it arrives.

corroy.name: Oppressor
corroy.gloss: tier-1 destroyer, plasma at 710 and seeker torpedoes; outranges every tier-1 ship and torpedo launcher, overrun by light ships
corroy.prose: The Oppressor is the tier-1 destroyer: 960 metal, 3950 health, speed 62, a 385-damage plasma cannon every 2.5 seconds at range 710 plus seeker torpedoes and 400 sonar. It outranges every tier-1 ship and the static torpedo launchers and kills submarines; lighter ships overrun it, so escort it with Supporters (coresupp) and a repair unit. Its wreck is worth protecting and reclaiming, since it is the dearest tier-1 ship.

corsala.name: Salamander
corsala.gloss: tier-2 amphibious heat-ray tank (speed 72), 164 dps at 340; raids from the water, no anti-air
corsala.prose: The Salamander is a fast amphibious tier-2 tank: 350 metal, 2100 health, speed 72, a heat ray doing 164 damage a second at range 340 that hits moving targets accurately. It walks the sea floor and climbs like a bot to raid from a beach the enemy is not watching, killing faster units its beam tracks; it has no anti-air, so EMP drones (corbw) and gunships kill it. A jammer near the beach hides it entering and leaving the water.

corsb.name: Dam Buster
corsb.air: 150 dps against aircraft, its full damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range
corsb.gloss: tier-1 seaplane bomber; skipping bombs bounce across water into ships and naval buildings; loses to fighters and flak
corsb.prose: The Dam Buster is a seaplane bomber: 200 metal, 940 health, speed 240, three 50-damage bombs every 8 seconds that skip across the water without exploding and can hit beyond the drop point. It hits slow ships, naval buildings and grouped units and makes surprise runs on a land base from the sea; fighters and flak kill it. Scout first and send fighters ahead.

corscreamer.name: Screamer
corscreamer.gloss: 1650-metal long-range anti-air, stockpiled missiles at 2400 with a blast nearly three times flak's; kills bombers before they arrive
corscreamer.prose: The Screamer is the long-range anti-air tower: 1650 metal and 32000 energy, 1670 health, stockpiled missiles at range 2400 with a blast nearly three times a flak burst's, one built every 14 seconds for 1800 energy, five stored. It kills strategic bombers and whole fighter walls before they reach the base; cheap scouts bait its shots, so set it to return fire or hold fire. It does nothing against ground.

corsd.name: Nemesis
corsd.gloss: 750-metal intrusion detector, pings moving cloaked and stealthy units within 2000 for 125 energy a second; guards the anti-nuke
corsd.prose: The Nemesis detects moving cloaked and radar-invisible units within 2000 by their vibration, terrain notwithstanding, for 750 metal and 6700 energy, 2800 health, 125 energy a second. It shows them as pings with a sound, not as targets, so units must be ordered onto them by hand; a standing cloaked unit is not seen. It is what protects a Prevailer (corfmd) from a Ghost's (armspy) EMP and a base from Gremlins (armgremlin). Only the tier-2 constructors build it.

corseah.name: Skyhook
corseah.gloss: tier-2 heavy assault transport; drops Sumos and Mammoths on the front line; survives light AA, dies to flak
corseah.prose: The Skyhook is the armoured heavy transport: 370 metal, 2200 health, speed 185, carries tier-2 units and tier-1 turrets. It puts slow units like the Sumo (corcan) and Mammoth (corsumo) on the front line instead of walking them there, and it survives missile turrets and light mobile anti-air better than the light transports; fighters, flak and heavy anti-air still kill it with its cargo. Scout the drop zone's anti-air first; a lost Skyhook is its cargo lost with it.

corseap.name: Monsoon
corseap.air: 4 dps against aircraft (4% of its ground damage)
corseap.gloss: tier-1 torpedo gunship seaplane; circles ships dropping homing torpedoes; kills subs, weak to anti-air
corseap.prose: The Monsoon is a torpedo gunship seaplane: 230 metal, 1000 health, speed 200, a 342-damage homing torpedo every 4 seconds at range 600, 535 sonar. It circles ships and submarines dropping torpedoes and works in narrow water where torpedo bombers miss, so it kills submarines without risking ships; it is cheaper than the Puffin (armseap) with less damage. Naval anti-air and fighters kill it.

corsent.name: Fury
corsent.gloss: tier-2 flak tank; wide-area flak at 775 kills groups of aircraft; nothing against ground
corsent.prose: The Fury is the tier-2 flak vehicle: 470 metal, 2700 health, speed 69, rapid flak at range 775 whose wide bursts kill tier-1 and most tier-2 aircraft in groups. It has no ground weapon and needs the army for cover; flak's range is shorter than missile anti-air but far better against a formation. Build it once enemy air has been seen.

corsfig.name: Bat
corsfig.gloss: tier-1 seaplane fighter, air-to-air missiles at 710; escorts bombers and ships, submerges to escape
corsfig.prose: The Bat is the seaplane fighter: 90 metal, 220 health, speed 316, guided anti-air missiles at range 710 that do nothing to ground. It escorts seaplane bombers and a fleet against enemy aircraft, faster than the Cyclone (armsfig) with less health, and it submerges to escape fighters or to ambush a bomber. Against the ground it is useless.

corsh.name: Goon
corsh.air: 12 dps against aircraft (19% of its ground damage)
corsh.gloss: 75-metal fast hovercraft raider, laser at 230; lands behind the line and swarms; dies to light towers
corsh.prose: The Goon is a cheap fast hovercraft: 75 metal, 255 health, speed 109.5, a 36-damage laser every 0.6 seconds at range 230. It crosses water and land alike, so a swarm lands behind the enemy's defensive line and raids the expansion there, and surrounded units take extra damage. A Sentry (armllt) or Guard (corllt) kills it, and so does any line unit.

corshad.name: Whirlwind
corshad.air: 93 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corshad.gloss: tier-1 bomber, five 112-damage bombs every 6 s; kills buildings and slow groups; loses to fighters and anti-air
corshad.prose: The Whirlwind is the tier-1 bomber: 150 metal, 680 health, speed 234, a run of five 112-damage bombs. It is for buildings and slow packed units, and a few level an undefended expansion; fighters and any anti-air kill it. Scout first, send Valiants (corveng) ahead to clear the fighter wall, and drag the attack order along the target's layout for a carpet run.

corshark.name: Predator
corshark.air: 159 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corshark.gloss: tier-2 fast submarine, homing torpedoes at 400; the submarine killer, hunts Serpents and Krakens; a few in every navy
corshark.prose: The Predator is the submarine killer: 730 metal, 1610 health, speed 84, a 350-damage homing torpedo every 2.2 seconds at range 400, 525 sonar, faster and more agile than other submarines with wider firing angles. It hunts enemy submarines, the battle subs above all, which otherwise kill an unguarded fleet, and it raids unguarded fleets itself. A few belong in every tier-2 navy.

corshiva.name: Shiva
corshiva.gloss: 1600-metal amphibious siege mech; plasma at 650 and a heavy rocket at 800; loses to Bulls and Pulsars
corshiva.prose: The Shiva is the cheapest Cortex gantry unit: 1600 metal, 9400 health, speed 48, a 600-damage plasma cannon at range 650 and a 750-damage vertical rocket at 800. It breaks defensive lines and lightly packed armies and walks the sea floor to arrive from the water. Heavy tanks like the Bull (armbull) and heavy turrets like the Pulsar (armanni) beat it, and its slow rocket lands where allies may have walked.

corshroud.name: Shroud
corshroud.gloss: 130-metal tier-2 jammer tower, hides everything within 700 from radar for 125 energy a second
corshroud.prose: The Shroud is the tier-2 jammer tower: 130 metal and 20000 energy, 890 health, hiding everything within 700 from enemy radar for 125 energy a second. It hides a whole base or a massed army from long-range weapons that target by radar; line of sight still sees through it. The tier-2 constructors and the Twitcher (corfast) build it.

corsilo.name: Apocalypse
corsilo.gloss: 7700-metal nuclear silo, stockpiles 15000-damage missiles at 187500 energy each; erases a base or an army; stopped by anti-nukes
corsilo.prose: The Apocalypse is the nuclear silo: 7700 metal and 82000 energy, 6200 health, stockpiling nuclear missiles that take 180 seconds and 187500 energy each, up to ten, with a wider blast than the Armageddon (armsilo) and a slower build. An anti-nuke covering the target stops it, unless several are fired at once or a Spectre (corspy) has stunned the anti-nuke first; aim at the edge of the anti-nuke's cover, where the wide blast still reaches. It is a decision of a whole tier-2 economy.

corsjam.name: Phantasm
corsjam.gloss: tier-2 radar jammer ship, hides units within 900 from enemy radar for 80 energy a second; unarmed
corsjam.prose: The Phantasm is the fleet's jammer: 280 metal, 1450 health, speed 40, everything within 900 of it hidden from enemy radar for 80 energy a second, no weapon. Put one among missile ships to move round a flank unseen, strike and escape; line of sight still sees the ships. It has no gun of its own and dies to anything that finds it, so it stays inside the fleet.

corsktl.name: Skuttle
corsktl.gloss: cloaked amphibious crawling bomb; the cloak gets it to the target; 755 metal, big blast
corsktl.prose: The Skuttle is the expensive crawling bomb: 755 metal, 355 health, speed 84, cloaked (15 energy a second standing, 40 moving) and amphibious, with a larger blast than the Bedbug (corroach). The cloak is its point: it walks unseen into a fusion cluster, a factory or a packed army and self-destructs. A Juno (corjuno) pulse that knocks out enemy radar first, and a Tracer or Nemesis on the enemy side, decide whether it arrives. Spread several out.

corsnap.name: Cayman
corsnap.air: 21 dps against aircraft (30% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corsnap.gloss: tier-1 hovertank, plasma at 370, 1720 health; crosses water to reinforce a fleet or a landing; hates bombers
corsnap.prose: The Cayman is a 300-metal hovertank: 1720 health, speed 67, a 98-damage plasma shot every 1.4 seconds at range 370. It moves over land and sea equally, so it fights beside ships or lands with a raid, and it is the line unit of a hovercraft force, with more health than the Crocodile (armanac) at more cost. Bombers kill it as they kill any tank, so bring anti-air.

corsok.name: Cataphract
corsok.air: 56 dps against aircraft (33% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corsok.gloss: 950-metal heavy laser hovertank; 750-damage laser at 725, 500 energy a shot; hits subs from the sea
corsok.prose: The Cataphract is a 950-metal hovercraft from the gantry: 4200 health, speed 45, a 750-damage laser cannon every 4.5 seconds at range 725 for 500 energy, plus a torpedo. It attacks a shore from the sea, outranges and outguns cruisers, ignores depth charges and kills submerged units with its torpedo without reply. It is not fast and it needs a lot of energy to fire.

corsolar.name: Solar Collector
corsolar.gloss: 20 energy a second for 150 metal and no energy to build; the safe generator from an empty store
corsolar.prose: The Solar Collector makes 20 energy a second for 150 metal and, unusually, no energy at all to build, with 355 health and 50 energy storage. That is why it is the first generator when the store is empty or a lab is about to draw 80 a second: it never stalls the builder. At 7.5 metal per energy a second it is dearer than wind on a windy map (Quicksilver averages 12) and cheaper than wind where the wind is weak; strong players build one solar and then wind. It closes when hit and loses its output while closed.

corspec.name: Deceiver
corspec.gloss: radar jammer bot, hides units within 450 from enemy radar for 80 energy a second; unarmed
corspec.prose: The Deceiver is a 75-metal jammer bot: everything within 450 of it is hidden from enemy radar, for 80 energy a second. It walks with a raiding party or an army so the enemy sees nothing on radar until the fight starts, and it hides Sheldons (cormort) and Arbiters (corhrk) from counter-fire; a Tracer (armsd) or Nemesis (corsd) sees through it. It has 350 health and no weapon.

corspy.name: Spectre
corspy.gloss: cloaked, radar-invisible spy; spots for artillery and self-destructs into an EMP burst; no weapon
corspy.prose: The Spectre is a 150-metal spy bot, cloaked and invisible to radar (15 energy a second standing, 40 moving), 450 health, no weapon. It walks into the enemy base to spot for artillery and can self-destruct in a 360-wide EMP burst that stuns everything around it for twenty seconds, which switches off an anti-nuke (Citadel, armamd) or a turret cluster long enough for an attack. A Tracer (armsd) or Nemesis (corsd) detects it and anything that sees it kills it. It can reclaim walls and, slowly, enemy buildings, uncloaked.

corssub.name: Kraken
corssub.air: 206 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corssub.gloss: tier-2 battle submarine, 1650-damage torpedoes at 850; kills heavy ships and tier-3 amphibians; loses to Predators
corssub.prose: The Kraken is the battle submarine: 1900 metal, 3900 health, speed 39, a 1650-damage homing torpedo every 8 seconds at range 850 (1110 against other subs), submerged and unseen without sonar. It kills battleships and heavy ships from beyond their reach and guards the sea against tier-3 amphibious units; submarine killers like the Predator (corshark) and Barracuda (armsubk) and torpedo launchers beat it. Never the whole fleet.

corstorm.name: Aggravator
corstorm.air: 41 dps against aircraft, its full damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range
corstorm.gloss: rocket bot that outranges light turrets (475 vs 435); slow rockets, loses to anything that closes
corstorm.prose: The Aggravator fires one 157-damage rocket every 3.8 seconds at range 475: 110 metal, 740 health, speed 48. It outranges a Guard (corllt) or Sentry (armllt), so a group held at range kills light turrets and what stands behind them, and it forces a commander back. Against moving units it is poor: the rocket is slow and unguided and barely leads its target, and in equal-metal duels it lost to every mobile unit it could not outrange; the Twin Guard (corhllt, 490) and heavy laser towers (620) outreach it. Screen it with Grunts (corak) or Thugs (corthud). It cannot hit aircraft.

corsub.name: Orca
corsub.air: 137 dps against aircraft, its full damage
corsub.gloss: tier-1 submarine, unguided torpedoes at 500; invisible without sonar, kills underwater extractors and unguarded fleets
corsub.prose: The Orca is the tier-1 submarine: 580 metal, 1060 health, speed 57, a 342-damage torpedo every 2.5 seconds at range 500, invisible to radar and to anything without sonar. One or two in a careless enemy's water kill underwater extractors and ships without anti-submarine weapons; anything with sonar and torpedoes kills it, since it has little health for its firepower. Sonar and other submarines see it, and a destroyer's torpedoes end it quickly.

corsumo.name: Mammoth
corsumo.air: 118 dps against aircraft (24% of its ground damage)
corsumo.gloss: 2200-metal walking wall: 15600 health, 503 dps beam at 650; the unit that breaks a tower line; speed 23
corsumo.prose: The Mammoth is the heaviest tier-2 bot: 2200 metal, 15600 health, speed 23, a beam laser doing 503 damage a second at range 650 for 75 energy a shot (125 a second at full rate). Its range barely exceeds the heavy laser towers (620) and it absorbs their fire while everything behind it kills, and in the simulated study a Mammoth behind a tier-1 screen was the one mix either faction had that reliably beat the opponent's minute-25 tower line (+0.25 to +0.41). It is so slow that a heavy transport is the usual way to the fight, and it needs energy to fire. Build it when a base has to be broken, not for the open field.

corsy.name: Shipyard
corsy.gloss: tier-1 shipyard on water, 450 metal; makes the construction ship, Herring, Supporter, Riptide, Oppressor, Orca, Death Cavalry
corsy.prose: The Shipyard is the tier-1 naval factory, built only on water: 450 metal and 950 energy, 4300 health, 150 build power, making the Construction Ship (corcs), Death Cavalry, Supporter, Herring, Riptide, Oppressor and Orca. It is offered only where the builder can reach water deep enough. On a land map there is no reason to build it.

cortarg.name: Pinpointer
cortarg.gloss: 800-metal targeting facility, halves radar-dot wobble for the whole team, 100 energy a second; three is plenty
cortarg.prose: The Pinpointer halves the wobble of radar dots for the whole team, for 800 metal and 7500 energy, 2000 health, and 100 energy a second. It is what lets Sheldons (cormort), Persecutors (cortoast), the Bulwark (cordoom) and the plasma batteries hit what radar shows without sight; a second and third stack with diminishing returns (75 and 87.5 percent), and three is plenty. Only the tier-2 constructors build it.

cortermite.name: Termite
cortermite.gloss: all-terrain tier-2 assault spider; 331 dps heat rays at 340, 60 energy a shot; climbs cliffs, slow
cortermite.prose: The Termite is an all-terrain assault spider: 540 metal, 3100 health, speed 50, twin heat rays doing 331 damage a second at range 340 with a small splash, for 60 energy a shot (about 75 a second at full rate). It climbs where tanks cannot and hits from the side of a hill the enemy did not fortify, and it takes only a fifth of EMP damage. On open ground the Sumo (corcan) is nearly always the better buy; the simulated study has Termite a close second (+0.46 to +0.58) to the Sumo mix. It loses to tanks and turrets that out-range it and to being slow in the open.

corthud.name: Thug
corthud.air: 12 dps against aircraft (20% of its ground damage, and only when nothing on the ground is in range)
corthud.gloss: the tier-1 line bot; plasma at 380, wins most equal-metal fights, loses to Pounders and kiting
corthud.prose: The Thug is the unit tier-1 Cortex fights with: 140 metal, 1100 health, speed 45, a 104-damage plasma shot every 1.7 seconds at range 380. In equal-metal duels head on it won most tier-1 matchups; it beats the Pawn (armpw) badly and the Grunt (corak), holds against the Mace (armham) with a slight loss, and overpowers light turrets. It loses to the Pounder (corlevlr), to artillery it cannot reach, and to fast units that refuse the fight; it is slow, so it anchors a line rather than chasing. Its plasma gains range from high ground. Build it as the default line unit, with Grunts for raiding and Aggravators (corstorm) for turrets.

cortide.name: Tidal Generator
cortide.gloss: 85-metal tidal generator on water; steady output set by the map's tide
cortide.prose: The Tidal Generator makes a steady amount of energy set by the map's tidal strength, for 85 metal and 250 energy, 395 health, built on water. Where the tide is good it is cheap steady energy for a sea base; on a land map it is not offered. Its output is fixed, unlike wind's.

cortitan.name: Angler
cortitan.air: 150 dps against aircraft, its full damage
cortitan.gloss: tier-2 torpedo bomber, 1200-damage homing torpedo; kills ships and submarines, nothing against land
cortitan.prose: The Angler is the torpedo bomber: 410 metal, 1960 health, speed 279, a 1200-damage homing torpedo every 8 seconds, with 800 sonar so it finds submerged targets alone. It does massive damage to ships, submarines and amphibious units and nothing to land targets. The torpedo needs a long open stretch of water; a run over the shoreline sticks it in the sand. Naval anti-air and fighters kill it.

cortl.name: Urchin
cortl.air: 187 dps against aircraft, its full damage
cortl.gloss: 170-metal offshore torpedo launcher, 187 dps at 500 against ships and subs; nothing against land or air
cortl.prose: The Urchin is the tier-1 torpedo launcher built on water: 170 metal and 1800 energy, 1440 health, a 280-damage torpedo every 1.5 seconds at range 500 with its own 400 sonar. It kills ships and submarines that come near and is the cheap defence of a sea base; it cannot hit land, air or hovercraft, and destroyers out-range it. It is offered only where the builder finds water, and it is the first defence a shipyard gets.

cortoast.name: Persecutor
cortoast.gloss: 2500-metal pop-up artillery, 420 damage at 1390; out-ranges the enemy's artillery and towers except vertical launchers
cortoast.prose: The Persecutor is the tier-2 pop-up plasma artillery: 2500 metal and 17000 energy, 4250 health, a 420-damage shell every 2.1 seconds at range 1390, a straight upgrade of the Agitator (corpun) in range, damage and rate. It kills the artillery units that threaten a front line and every tower but the long-range cannons; vertical-launch platforms out-range it. It sees nothing of what it shoots at, so it needs radar and a Pinpointer (cortarg), and a hill extends its range.

cortrem.name: Tremor
cortrem.gloss: tier-2 heavy artillery, 200-damage shells twice a second at 1470 over walls and hills; carpets an area; friendly-fire hazard
cortrem.prose: The Tremor fires 200-damage high-arc shells twice a second to range 1470: 1850 metal, 3000 health, speed 40.5. It carpets an area, over walls and cliffs, and outranges everything but the long-range cannons, so it kills masses of light units and slow fragile ones, Sharpshooters (armsnipe) and Mausers (armmart); its shells land on friends too, so aim it by hand. Anything that gets close kills it; high ground extends its range.

cortron.name: Catalyst
cortron.gloss: 1200-metal tactical missile launcher, stockpiled 4000-damage missiles with a 380 blast at 2250; strips defences before an assault
cortron.prose: The Catalyst is a stockpiling tactical missile launcher: 1200 metal and 14000 energy, 3550 health, missiles with range 2250 doing 4000 damage in a 380-wide blast, each 550 metal and 17437 energy and 75 seconds, up to ten stored and fired two seconds apart. It obliterates a turret cluster or a packed army before an assault, hits submerged units, and gives the enemy no launch warning. It is fired by hand.

coruwadves.name: Hardened Energy Storage
coruwadves.gloss: tier-2 hardened storage, 40000 energy for 840 metal, 12700 health; the bank for stockpile weapons and gantries
coruwadves.prose: The Hardened Energy Storage adds 40000 energy storage for 840 metal and 11000 energy, with 12700 health. It is the bank that a nuclear silo, a Bulwark (cordoom) or a long-range cannon draws on, and it lets a big economy ride a stall; the tier-2 constructors build it on land or water. Its health makes it the storage that survives a raid, so the bank is still there when the enemy leaves.

coruwadvms.name: Hardened Metal Storage
coruwadvms.gloss: tier-2 hardened storage, 10000 metal for 760 metal, 11200 health
coruwadvms.prose: The Hardened Metal Storage adds 10000 metal storage for 760 metal and 11000 energy, with 11200 health. It is for a tier-2 economy that banks for gantry units and long-range guns; the tier-2 constructors build it on land or water. It is a late buy: at tier 1 a full metal store means a second lab, not a bigger store.

coruwageo.name: Advanced Geothermal Powerplant
coruwageo.gloss: tier-2 geothermal on an underwater vent, 1250 energy a second for 1500 metal
coruwageo.prose: The underwater Advanced Geothermal Powerplant is the Advanced Geothermal Powerplant (corageo) for a vent under water: 1250 energy a second for 1500 metal and 27000 energy, 4150 health, 12000 energy storage, with the same base-levelling explosion. Only a builder that works under water places it. It is the most metal-efficient energy a sea base can build, and the most dangerous to stand near.

coruwes.name: Naval Energy Storage
coruwes.gloss: 6000 energy storage built under water for 175 metal
coruwes.prose: The Naval Energy Storage is the Energy Storage (corestor) built on the sea floor: 6000 energy storage for 175 metal and 1800 energy, 2000 health. It explodes when destroyed. Only a builder that works under water places it.

coruwfus.name: Naval Fusion Reactor
coruwfus.gloss: tier-2 fusion on water, 1220 energy a second for 5400 metal; hides energy under the sea
coruwfus.prose: The Naval Fusion Reactor is the water-built fusion: 1220 energy a second for 5400 metal and 34000 energy, 5900 health, 2500 energy storage. It is the energy of a sea base and a way to keep energy out of a land raid's reach; it explodes when destroyed. Only the Advanced Construction Sub (coracsub) builds it.

coruwgeo.name: Offshore Geothermal Powerplant
coruwgeo.gloss: 300 energy a second on an underwater steam vent, 540 metal
coruwgeo.prose: The Offshore Geothermal Powerplant is the Geothermal Powerplant (corgeo) for a vent under water: 300 energy a second for 540 metal and 13000 energy, 2050 health. Only a builder that works under water places it. It gives a sea base the same steady energy as the land plant, and explodes the same way when killed.

coruwmme.name: Naval Advanced Metal Extractor
coruwmme.gloss: tier-2 extractor upgrade for an underwater spot, 640 metal, four times the yield
coruwmme.prose: The Naval Advanced Metal Extractor is the Advanced Metal Extractor (cormoho) for a spot under water: 640 metal and 8100 energy, 3900 health, four times the spot's yield, 20 energy a second upkeep, 600 metal storage. The Advanced Construction Sub (coracsub) builds it on a claimed underwater spot. Like the land upgrade it repays its metal in about 100 seconds and draws 20 energy a second.

coruwmmm.name: Naval Advanced Energy Converter
coruwmmm.gloss: the tier-2 converter on water, 600 energy a second into 10.3 metal for 370 metal
coruwmmm.prose: The Naval Advanced Energy Converter is the Advanced Energy Converter (cormmkr) built on water: 600 energy a second into 10.3 metal a second for 370 metal and 21000 energy, 560 health. It is for a sea base's energy surplus, and it chains explosions when clustered. Only the Advanced Construction Sub (coracsub) builds it, and only the tier-2 sea economy has the surplus to feed it.

coruwms.name: Naval Metal Storage
coruwms.gloss: 3000 metal storage built under water for 340 metal
coruwms.prose: The Naval Metal Storage is the Metal Storage (cormstor) built on the sea floor: 3000 metal storage for 340 metal and 590 energy, 2100 health. Only a builder that works under water places it. It explodes when destroyed, like the land store.

corvalk.name: Hercules
corvalk.gloss: tier-1 light air transport; carries one tier-1 or light tier-2 land unit, not the commander; dies to anti-air
corvalk.prose: The Hercules is the light transport: 74 metal, 280 health, speed 198, carries one land unit of tier 1 or light tier 2, not the commander and not heavies like the Tzar (corgol). It drops units past a defensive line, moves a constructor to a far spot, and lifts a Construction Turret (cornanotc) to wherever build power is needed. Scout for anti-air first; anything that shoots air kills it and its cargo.

corvamp.name: Nighthawk
corvamp.gloss: tier-2 stealth fighter, speed 379, missiles at 690; invisible to radar; the air-superiority unit
corvamp.prose: The Nighthawk is the tier-2 fighter: 145 metal, 290 health, speed 379, guided missiles at range 690 for aircraft, invisible to radar so the enemy cannot count them. It kills heavy aircraft and groups of them, and paired with a bombing run it clears the air defence ahead of the bombers; it is faster and more fragile than the Highwind (armhawk). It cannot usefully hit ground.

corveng.name: Valiant
corveng.gloss: tier-1 fighter, speed 298, missiles at 680 against aircraft only; the answer to enemy air, useless against ground
corveng.prose: The Valiant is the tier-1 fighter: 73 metal, 156 health, speed 298, a guided missile at range 680 that hurts only aircraft. It reaches any part of the map, so a patrol in front of the base stops scouts, gunships and bombers, and sent ahead of a bombing run it breaks the enemy's fighter wall. It cannot hit ground. Build them once enemy aircraft have been seen.

corvipe.name: Scorpion
corvipe.gloss: 730-metal pop-up sabot battery, 825 damage every 2 s at 730; kills raiders and heavies alike, retracts under fire
corvipe.prose: The Scorpion is the tier-2 pop-up sabot rocket battery: 730 metal and 14000 energy, 3000 health, an 825-damage rocket every 2 seconds (413 a second) at range 730, for a relatively low cost. It kills fast low-health raiders and skirmishers and hurts heavy units, and switched off it retracts to soak artillery; repairs on it are far more efficient while it is down, so a construction turret beside it pays. Artillery that out-ranges 730 beats it in the end.

corvoyr.name: Augur
corvoyr.gloss: mobile radar bot, 2200 radar and 925 sight; lets mortars and artillery use their range; unarmed
corvoyr.prose: The Augur is a 99-metal radar bot with 2200 radar range and 925 sight, 390 health, no weapon. It shows the enemy to units that fire further than they see, Sheldons (cormort), Arbiters (corhrk), artillery and plasma batteries, and its big sight radius makes the Sheldon's shells land. One behind an army turns range into hits; any raider that reaches it kills it.

corvp.name: Vehicle Plant
corvp.gloss: tier-1 vehicle plant, 570 metal; makes the constructor vehicle, Rascal, Incisor, Brute, Pounder, Wolverine, Lasher, Garpike, Muskrat, Trapper
corvp.prose: The Vehicle Plant is the tier-1 vehicle factory: 570 metal and 1550 energy, 3000 health, 150 build power, ten units: Construction Vehicle (corcv), Muskrat, Trapper, Rascal, Incisor, Garpike, Brute, Pounder, Wolverine and Lasher. Vehicles are faster on flat ground, tougher and dearer than bots and climb worse; the plant is where the Pounder, the strongest tier-1 land unit in a straight fight, and the tier-1 artillery come from, and strong players favour it on large open maps. It costs more than the bot lab and draws more energy while building, so it is usually the second factory.

corvrad.name: Omen
corvrad.gloss: tier-2 radar vehicle, 2200 radar and 900 sight; lets artillery use its range; unarmed and slow
corvrad.prose: The Omen is a 100-metal radar vehicle: 2200 radar range, 900 sight, 570 health, no weapon, slower than the Prophet (armseer). It shows the enemy to Quakers (cormart), Tremors (cortrem), Lashers (cormist) and plasma batteries; an artillery group without one wastes its range. Keep it a little behind the line.

corvroc.name: Negotiator
corvroc.gloss: stealthy siege rocket truck, 1700 damage at 1310 every 16 s over walls; kills fortifications; useless against movers
corvroc.prose: The Negotiator lobs a 1700-damage rocket on a high arc to range 1310 every 16 seconds: 880 metal, 1390 health, speed 33, invisible to radar. It kills turrets, batteries and fortified buildings behind walls from beyond their reach, and its splash hurts packed units; against anything mobile it is helpless. Escort it and spot for it.

corwin.name: Wind Turbine
corwin.gloss: 43-metal wind generator; output follows the map's wind (the picture's economy line says this map's average); costs energy to build
corwin.prose: The Wind Turbine makes whatever the wind gives, up to 25 energy a second, for 43 metal and 175 energy, 220 health. On a windy map it is the cheapest energy there is (about 3.5 metal per energy a second at an average of 12) and the bulk of a tier-1 economy; where the wind is weak the Solar Collector (corsolar) is the better buy. It costs energy to build, so a first turbine from an empty store stalls, and its output swings minute to minute, which is what storage and a solar or two are for.

corwolv.name: Wolverine
corwolv.gloss: tier-1 artillery, 710 range outranges every tier-1 tower; 750 health, blind past 330, needs a spotter and a screen
corwolv.prose: The Wolverine is the tier-1 artillery: 170 metal, 750 health, speed 48, a 300-damage shell every 7.1 seconds lobbed to range 710, more than the heavy laser towers (620). It kills turrets from where they cannot answer; it fires only over its front, is inaccurate against anything moving, and sees only 330, so alone it walks into a turret's range before it sees it. It needs a Rascal (corfav) or radar to spot and Pounders (corlevlr) or Brutes (corraid) in front, and it is never an answer to units.
